name: locate
description: Quickly finds files by name using a prebuilt database maintained by updatedb, far faster than find for whole-disk searches.

flags.description: Print only the count of matches.
Print only files that currently exist on disk.
Interpret the pattern as a basic regular expression.

examples.explanation: Searches the database and prints every path containing nginx.conf.
Counts matching entries without printing them.
Case-insensitive search for readme, showing the first five results.

about: locate reads from an index (for mlocate: /var/lib/mlocate/mlocate.db) refreshed by updatedb, usually daily via cron or a systemd timer. Results may include files deleted since the last update, and brand-new files will not appear until the next refresh. Run sudo updatedb to refresh immediately.
mlocate restricts results to files the invoking user can see, based on directory permissions recorded in the database.
useCases: Checking where a package installed its files.
mistakes: Expecting a just-created file to appear — the database is not real-time.
Using locate on systems where the mlocate/plocate package is not installed (minimal containers often lack it).
distroNotes: Modern distributions ship plocate or mlocate; both provide the locate command. plocate is faster and uses a different index but the same interface.
